text:
maria: heads-up — saw a latency spike on the nightly perf run around 02:00 UTC, looks correlated with a kernel swap during batch formation.
kevin: ugh, saw that too. profiler shows FlashAttention falling back for a subset of small-seq requests, which bloats the queue.
ashley: can you paste the quick flame? curious which op fell back.
maria: here — pasted the trimmed trace:```
small_seq_worker: new batch formed (N=12, tokens=210)
kernel_probe: choose=flash_attn_v2 if seq<=64 else hybrid_attn
flash_init: memcheck failed for buf alloc -> fallback to generic_attn
batch_commit: batch_size -> 24 (queued waiting 120ms)
```
devon: memcheck failed means our allocator returned null on the scratch buffer. that's probably the tiled-kv allocator hitting a fragmentation case.
kevin: exactly. paged-KV reclaims async pages and we saw a 3x latency variance when reclaim coincides with batch sealing. The result: small seqs that would pick Flash get generic instead, but form larger batches to amortize cost -> latency spike.
ashley: rough numbers from profiling: Flash path avg 6ms/token, generic 14ms/token. When fallback happened the median latency for interactive workload went from 120ms -> 340ms.
maria: here's the RL config we used for the test: `batcher.max_wait_ms=50, token_budget_target=256, kernel_probe.enabled=true`
kevin: proposal: add a fast-path in the batch formation: if kernel_probe suspects flash may fail due to scratch pressure, force tight token_budget_target for small-seq buckets (e.g., 96 -> 64) to keep batches small and avoid accumulative fallback.
devon: or we could make the probe itself non-blocking: try ephemeral allocation during probe and if it indicates low headroom, mark node 'flash_unavailable' for the next 1s then route to hybrid kernel proactively. cheaper than larger batch latencies.
ashley: I like the ephemeral probe but worried about noisy toggles. maybe combine with exponential backoff and per-GPU counters.
kevin: agreed. Also we should update the allocator to favor contiguous scratch for flash kernels — increase max contiguous arena when >50% of queued small-seq requests exist. Could be a quick win.
maria: action items: 1) devon to add ephemeral probe + cooldown flag (PR draft by EOD) 2) kevin to add a metrics tag `kernel_probe.scratch_pressure` and dashboard panel 3) ashley to run a replay with tightened token_budget_target for small-seq and compare p99.
devon: starting on probe now. will instrument logs as `probe:flash=ok|fail reason=` and add a counter.
ashley: putting a replay job in `perf/replays/interactive-smallseq` with `token_budget_target=96` and `batcher.max_wait_ms=30` — will post results.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: runtime/allocator patch -> staging at 2026-03-10T06:30:00Z (job id rf-2246).
kevin: one more thought — kernel selection policy should include a heuristic for 'queued batch variance'. if variance high, prefer stable kernels even if slightly slower to keep SLOs. we need an escape hatch to trade token cost for latency variance.
maria: good suggestion. will add to the design doc: `/docs/runtime/kernel-policy.md` (WIP).
kevin: short-term we should patch the probe to emit the reason string so we can triage whether it's fragmentation or transient OOM.
devon: yep. I'll add `reason=frag|oom|temp` and the page size snapshots.
ashley: replay results attached: p50 110ms, p95 220ms, p99 380ms for baseline; with tightened token_budget_target p99 dropped to 210ms. big improvement but cost up ~8%. detailed numbers in the thread gist -> https://gist.github.com/rw-perf/abcd1234
maria: thanks. let's land ephemeral probe + metrics, then iterate on allocator tuning. small doc update and a canary on staging.
kevin: will follow up with a short postmortem note if the staging canary shows improvement. :thumbsup:
